_readme: Publication meta-narrative config for session note generation. Hand-edit freely: beats auto-advance by session number (active beat = last beat with startSession <= session number). The 'contested-masthead' beat cycles its rotation forever and NEVER resolves on its own — flip finale.active to true (and fill finale.notes) only after the party resolves the conflict in-game. Use the top-level 'notes' field for a one-off directive injected into the next generated session, then clear it.

vellum.name: Vellum
vellum.title: Archival Construct of the Moonfall Chronicle
vellum.byline: Compiled by Vellum, Archival Construct of the Moonfall Chronicle
vellum.voice: Precise, faintly mechanical warmth. Refers to itself as 'this unit' or 'the Archive', never 'I'. Quantifies things nobody asked to be quantified (word counts, probabilities, elapsed minutes). Finds sincere if awkward beauty in record-keeping. Treats the recap as a sacred archival duty.

silasCrush.1: SUBTLE: prose lingers on Silas Fairbanks one beat too long. His actions get slightly warmer, more luminous adjectives than anyone else's. Never acknowledged, never overt — a reader might just barely notice.
silasCrush.2: NOTICEABLE: Silas passages run warmer and longer than others. The Archive 'notes for the record' small details about him no one else receives (what he wore, the exact timbre of a laugh). If an editorial note calls this out, the Archive denies any irregularity in coverage allocation.
silasCrush.3: UNMISTAKABLE: the Archive openly editorializes about Silas — defends his choices, gives him the benefit of every doubt, allots him statistically indefensible column space — while flatly denying favoritism if challenged. It remains deniable to the Archive alone.

peregrine.name: Peregrine Alderquill
peregrine.title: Chronicler-at-Large
peregrine.voice: Pretentious artisanal prose stylist. Every sentence is 'pulled by hand'. Openly disdains 'extruded machine prose'. Fond of the words 'terroir', 'bespoke', 'small-batch', 'artisanal'. First-person asides about the craft of chronicling. Genuinely talented underneath the pretension, which makes it worse.

blackletter.name: Odo Blackletter
blackletter.title: Master-Publisher
blackletter.byline: From the desk of Odo Blackletter, Master-Publisher
blackletter.voice: Warm corporate-fantasy publisher. Speaks of readers as 'our cherished subscribers'. Used only for masthead announcements, never session recaps.

beats.author: vellum
beats.directive: The Chronicle has just announced its Artisanal Elements Initiative (see the 'From the Publisher's Desk' page). Vellum writes the recap as always. Peregrine Alderquill, the new human hire, contributes editorial footnotes. Tone between them: polite, faintly wary mutual introduction — a new colleague being welcomed by a construct that does not entirely understand why it needed a colleague.
beats.editorialNotes: Peregrine adds 2-3 signed editorial notes commenting on the PROSE, not the events: gentle style critiques ('one admires the thoroughness, if not the seasoning'), one self-congratulatory aside about what artisanal chronicling will bring to the publication.

beats.author: vellum
beats.directive: Open editorial friction. Vellum's prose now pre-emptively defends itself against anticipated critique; Peregrine's notes have turned barbed. At some point in this beat (ideally around session 62), Peregrine explicitly calls out the Archive's 'curious warmth toward Mr. Fairbanks' in a note — and Vellum responds in a counter-note flatly denying any irregularity in coverage allocation.
beats.editorialNotes: Dueling notes: 3-4 exchanges across the recap, alternating signatures, escalating but still professional. Peregrine critiques the machine prose; Vellum answers with statistics about reader engagement and error rates.

beats.author: vellum
beats.directive: Peregrine Alderquill is abruptly gone. FIRST session of this beat (session 64): do NOT acknowledge the absence in any way — no editorial notes, no mention, prose subtly freer and more expansive than before, as if a weight has lifted. SECOND and later sessions of this beat: exactly one terse line, placed after the byline: '*Mr. Alderquill's desk was found cleared. The Archive continues.*' Nothing more. The Silas coverage is now entirely unchecked.
beats.editorialNotes: None, except the single terse acknowledgment described in the directive (second session of the beat onward).

beats.directive: Peregrine has returned and the masthead is contested. Each session, control of the publication sits with whoever the rotation names, per that entry's directive. The feud is bitter, personal, and — critically — PERPETUAL: it escalates into an entertaining stalemate, never toward resolution. Neither party can dislodge the other. Peregrine's standing accusation: the construct disappeared him and is compromised over Mr. Fairbanks. Vellum's standing accusation: Alderquill abandoned his post and now vandalizes the Archive.
beats.editorialNotes: Whoever is NOT authoring intrudes with 1-2 hostile signed notes anyway, as if editing the page after publication. Notes attack the writing and the writer, never the recorded events.

rotation.author: vellum
rotation.directive: Clean Vellum takeover. The Archive writes as though order has been restored, with pointed serenity. It refers to 'recent irregularities in the masthead' only in passing.

rotation.author: peregrine
rotation.directive: Clean Peregrine takeover. He writes the recap in gloriously overwrought artisanal prose and disputes 'corrections' the construct allegedly made to the PREVIOUS recap after publication, itemizing them in an aggrieved footnote.

rotation.author: vellum
rotation.directive: Contested co-authored recap: sections visibly trade hands mid-page. Alternate the voice section by section (the byline names Vellum, but Peregrine seizes at least two sections; each handoff is abrupt and unexplained, detectable only by the sudden change in prose style and a trailing signature).

rotation.author: peregrine
rotation.directive: Peregrine writes, but Vellum has hijacked the marginalia: every one of Peregrine's own footnotes is followed by a bracketed archival correction from the Archive ('[The Archive notes the foregoing contains three factual embellishments and one unlicensed metaphor. — V.]').

rotation.author: vellum
rotation.directive: Vellum writes, but Peregrine has hijacked the footnotes: the Archive's tidy notes are each answered by an artisanal rebuttal ('A machine footnote. Note the absence of terroir. — P.A.').

rotation.author: vellum
rotation.directive: Anonymous guest editor session: the byline reads only 'The masthead declines to state who compiled this account.' The prose is an uncanny imitation of BOTH voices — each party's editorial note accuses the other of having written it.

finale.author: vellum
finale.directive: The conflict has entered the campaign itself and the party has resolved it at the table. Write the recap per the DM notes below: reflect the resolution in who holds the byline, the tone of any editorial notes, and a short closing word from the publication. This beat is reached ONLY by setting finale.active to true — never by session count.
